subLocations.lore:
History
During the Spellplague of 1385 DR, the walking statue appeared and rampaged through the city. When the statues were stopped, she fell onto her side, where she still lay by 1492 DR.[

Description
It resembled a noble woman asleep in a garden. She bore the appearance of a female elf and, while active, her clothing and hair appeared to move naturally
subLocations.name: the lady dreaming
Street of Lances
subLocations.lore: Street of Lances was walked by broadcryers who peddled their broadsheets to passers-by.

subLocations.name: Seawind Alley
subLocations.lore: Seawind Alley was an alley notable for the ghostly voices that could be heard within the alley.

subLocations.name: Ghostwalk
subLocations.lore: Ghostwalk was considered sufficiently safe for the rich inhabitants of the ward to walk by undisturbed. Like other alleys in the Sea Ward, it was clean and wide. It contained numerous shadowtops that were favored by children to climb and play by.

subLocations.name: Westwall Street
subLocations.lore: Westwall Street was located in the western section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward, fully spanning the entire western boundary of the ward with the exterior wall in that portion of the city.

subLocations.name: Heroes' Walk
subLocations.lore: Every year during the summer, Heroes' Garden and Heroes' Walk were both overtaken by the nobles of the Church of Siamorphe on their holy day, the Divine Pageantry.

subLocations.name: Heroes' Garden
subLocations.lore: Heroes' Garden was one of the only public gardens in the city besides the City of the Dead.

subLocations.name: Trollkill Street
subLocations.lore: Trollkill Street was a large road in the city of Waterdeep, spanning nearly the whole northern portion of the Trollwall, that started in the Sea Ward and ended in the North Ward.

subLocations.name: Street of the Singing Dolphin
subLocations.lore: The Street of the Singing Dolphin was located in the western section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward. The road spanned the entire western side of the ward

subLocations.name: Oar Alley
subLocations.lore: A minor avenue of hard-packed earth and [[gravel]] that extended off of [[Ship Street]] and terminated in a dead end.

subLocations.name: New Olamn
subLocations.lore: The College of New Olamn, simply known as New Olamn, was a traditional bardic college

subLocations.name: Sahuagin Humbled
subLocations.lore: The [[Walking Statue of Waterdeep]] known as the Sahuagin Humbled was originally the only Walking Statue visible in Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: Deepwater Harbor
subLocations.lore: Thanks to continuous efforts by the [[Guild of Watermen]] and its [[merfolk]] population, the cold waters of Deepwater Harbor were exceptionally clean.

subLocations.name: Deepwater Isle
subLocations.lore: Deepwater was the largest in a ring of islands that enclosed and protected [[Deepwater Harbor]].

subLocations.name: T'Quession
subLocations.lore: T'Quession was a [[sea elf]] hamlet.

subLocations.name: Naval Harbor
subLocations.lore: The fleet of Waterdeep's navy was based in the Naval Harbor. Commercial and personal vessels were not permitted in this area.

subLocations.name: Philosopher's Court
subLocations.lore: Also known as the Foolsquare

subLocations.name: Burdag Lane
subLocations.lore: An entrance to the sewers of Waterdeep could be found on the intersection of Burdag Lane and Tsarnen Alley.

subLocations.name: Tsarnen Alley
subLocations.lore: Tsarnen Alley was a short, hard-packed dirt and gravel paved, alleyway. It was frequently walked down by pilgrims and priests on their way to the [[Plinth]].

subLocations.name: River Square
subLocations.lore: River Square was a hard-packed dirt and gravel courtyard.

subLocations.name: Tornsar Alley
subLocations.lore: Tornsar Alley was a small side alley.

subLocations.name: Juth Alley
subLocations.lore: Juth Alley was a small side alley.

subLocations.name: Shipwright's Square
subLocations.lore: Shipwright's Square was a small courtyard.

subLocations.name: Ghemmer's Alley
subLocations.lore: Ghemmer's Alley was a small backalley.

subLocations.name: Dancing Court
subLocations.lore: The Dancing Court was a cul-de-sac.

subLocations.name: The Boomgarden
subLocations.lore: The Boomgarden was a cul-de-sac, paved in hard-packed earth and gravel.

subLocations.name: Anchoret's Court
subLocations.lore: Anchoret's Court was a small courtyard.

subLocations.name: Sethma's Court
subLocations.lore: Sethma's Court was a cobbled courtyard.

subLocations.name: The Jar
subLocations.lore: The Jar was a small courtyard.

subLocations.name: Warriors' Monument
subLocations.lore: Warriors' Monument, also occasionally known as the Warriors of Waterdeep, was a monument in Waterdeep's [[City of the Dead]] meant to honor all those who ever fought to defend the city.

subLocations.name: Tuckpurse Alley
subLocations.lore: Tuckpurse Alley was an alleyway of hard-packed dirt and gravel.

subLocations.name: Gaustus Street
subLocations.lore:
Gaustus Street was a street of hard-packed dirt and gravel.

This street stretched from north to south, curving off of the [[Wall Way]] and terminating at the [[Court of the White Bull]].

subLocations.name: Walltower Walk
subLocations.lore: Walltower Walk was a street of hard-packed dirt and gravel.

subLocations.name: Urcandle Alley
subLocations.lore: Urcandle Alley was a short alleyway of hard-packed dirt and gravel. Urcandle Alley was home to one of the greatest concentrations of wheelwright stores in Waterdeep.

subLocations.name: Cliffwatch
subLocations.lore: The Cliffwatch was a public walkway.

subLocations.name: Sprangalar's Swordcut
subLocations.lore: Sprangalar's Swordcut, which was also simply called the Swordcut, was a small alley.

subLocations.name: Howling Cat Court
subLocations.lore: Howling Cat Court was a small courtyard.

subLocations.name: Mud Flats
subLocations.lore: The beach was frequented mostly by fishers, clam diggers, and occasional locals who enjoyed bathing in the cold waters of the [[Sea of Swords]].

subLocations.name: Tharqualnaar
subLocations.lore: Tharqualnaar was a village of [[merfolk]] in Deepwater Harbor in Waterdeep, beneath Deepwater Isle.

subLocations.name: Market
subLocations.lore: The largest open area within the city was the marketplace between Trader's Way and Bazaar street. It was full of merchants carts and stalls both day and night and was the best place in the city to find a good price for any trade good found in Faerûn, assuming one had some skill at haggling.

subLocations.name: Belzer's Walk
subLocations.lore: An alleyway that stood on the boundary line of the [[Waterdeep/Southern Ward|Southern Ward]] and [[Waterdeep/Trades Ward|Trades Ward]].

subLocations.name: Gull Leap
subLocations.lore: A cliff along the northwestern edge of Waterdeep, just outside the Trollwall, that was named in part for the significant amount of [[sea gull]]s that nested upon it.
